title: The First Climate Filing That Still Counts
subtitle: California SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 reports are targeted for 10 November 2026. The SEC has proposed rescinding its 2024 climate rules. A dual-listed metals CFO must file one and explain why the other no longer binds.
category: ESG Disclosure, Climate Risk & CFO Judgment
description: HBS-style teaching case dated 24 September 2026. Public facts: Jones Day (8 September 2026) maps U.S. climate rules as Rescinded / Required / Pending. SEC proposed full rescission of the March 2024 climate rules (Release 33-11421, 29 May 2026); comment period closed 3 August 2026; 31 August 2026 status report to the Eighth Circuit said staff were still reviewing more than 19,000 comments. Until a final rescission is adopted the 2024 rules remain stayed and the 2010 interpretive guidance continues. California SB 253 requires first Scope 1 and Scope 2 reports in 2026, currently targeted for 10 November 2026 pending completing regulation. CARB released additional reporting resources on 1 September 2026. CSRD and IFRS S2 remain binding for many groups with EU or ISSB-aligned listings. Composite firm: Pacific Deccan Metals Ltd. Composite decision-maker: CFO Meera Rao.
thumbnail: SEC MAY DROP FEDERAL CLIMATE RULES. CALIFORNIA STILL WANTS SCOPE 1 AND 2 BY 10 NOVEMBER 2026.
